facts.text: The little raven is completely black, with black feathers, beak and legs, and its adult eyes are white.
facts.quote: with completely black plumage, beak, and legs; as with all Australian species of Corvus, the black feathers have a grey base, and the iris of the adult bird is white

facts.text: Young little ravens change eye colour as they grow: nestlings have blue-grey eyes, juveniles brown, and immatures hazel with blue eyerings.
facts.quote: nestlings up to three months old have blue-grey eyes, juveniles aged from three to eleven months have brown eyes, and immature birds have hazel eyes with blue eyerings around the pupil

facts.text: It is a sociable bird that often forms large flocks which roam widely in search of food.
facts.quote: The little raven is a somewhat more sociable species than the Australian raven, often forming large flocks that roam freely over wide areas in search of food.

facts.text: Little ravens often nest in loose colonies of up to fifteen pairs, with nests only a few metres apart.
facts.quote: Little ravens often nest in a loose colony of up to fifteen pairs, with nests few metres apart.

facts.text: Both parents build the thin cup nest of sticks, with the male bringing material while the female lines the bowl with feathers.
facts.quote: Both birds build the nest, with the female taking over the lining of the nest while the male brings her material.

facts.text: Little ravens eat many ground-dwelling invertebrates such as spiders, grasshoppers and centipedes, which they behead before eating.
facts.quote: Common invertebrates eaten include spiders, millipedes, centipedes (which ravens behead before eating), grasshoppers, cicadas and caterpillars

facts.text: These intelligent birds have been recorded using tools and finding innovative ways to seek out food.
facts.quote: Little ravens are intelligent birds, and have been recorded using tools as well as having innovative methods of seeking out food.

facts.text: The little raven gives a harsh, guttural "kar-kar-kar-karrr" or "ark-ark-ark-arrk" call.
facts.quote: Its call is a harsh, guttural "kar-kar-kar-karrr" or "ark-ark-ark-arrk"

facts.text: Like all corvids, the little raven is capable of vocal mimicry, though this is mostly recorded in captivity.
facts.quote: Like all corvids, the little raven is capable of vocal mimicry, but this behavior is mostly recorded in captivity and only rarely in the wild.

facts.text: A clutch can hold up to six eggs, though usually four or five are laid.
facts.quote: A clutch can comprise up to six eggs, though usually four or five are laid
